patterns.description: Natural guitar key with open strings. The flat 2nd (F natural) against the open E root creates the signature Phrygian tension.
patterns.fretDiagram: Uses open strings and first 3 frets, strings 6-1

patterns.description: Moveable box pattern starting on the 5th fret, ideal for metal and fusion soloing across the neck.
Higher register position for expressive lead work and dark melodic phrasing in progressive and metal contexts.

commonPositions.usage: Progressive rock, higher register lead work

diatonicChords.function: Tonic - Dark minor center with exotic coloring from the flat 2nd
Supertonic - Characteristic Phrygian chord, the major flat-II creates the signature sound
Mediant - Relative major, bright contrast to the dark tonic
Dominant - Diminished quality, weak dominant adds to the modal instability
Submediant - Major chord providing harmonic color and contrast
Subtonic - Minor subtonic chord, supports modal cadences

commonProgressions.name: Phrygian Vamp (i-♭II)
commonProgressions.description: The signature Phrygian movement - the half-step motion between the minor tonic and major flat-II creates the iconic Spanish/exotic sound

commonProgressions.name: Andalusian Cadence (i-♭VII-♭VI-♭II)
commonProgressions.description: Classic descending Phrygian cadence widely used in flamenco and Spanish guitar, resolving to the characteristic flat-II

commonProgressions.name: Dark Metal Riff (i-♭II-♭III-♭II)
commonProgressions.description: Heavy metal-style progression exploiting the dark Phrygian tonality with power chord movement around the flat 2nd

practiceExercises.name: E Phrygian Scale Runs
practiceExercises.description: Practice the E Phrygian scale ascending and descending in open position, focusing on the characteristic flat 2nd interval
instructions: Start slowly with metronome at 60 BPM
Listen for the half-step between E and F that defines the Phrygian sound
Compare with E natural minor to hear the distinctive flat 2nd difference

practiceExercises.name: Phrygian Flamenco Phrase
practiceExercises.description: Practice a flamenco-style phrase using Phrygian mode over the i-bII vamp to develop authentic Spanish guitar phrasing
instructions: Play over an Em-F backing track or chord vamp
Emphasize the half-step movement between E and F for authentic Phrygian flavor
Add rasgueado-style strumming accents for flamenco authenticity

practiceExercises.name: Phrygian vs Natural Minor Ear Training
practiceExercises.description: Compare Phrygian with natural minor to hear the characteristic flat 2nd that creates the exotic, Spanish flavor
instructions: Play E Phrygian, then E natural minor back to back
Focus on the 2nd degree difference (F natural vs F# in E)
Sing both scales to internalize the distinctive Phrygian darkness

relatedScales.differences: Phrygian has a flat 2nd instead of natural 2nd - this is the only difference
relatedScales.usage: Standard minor sound without the exotic Phrygian darkness

relatedScales.differences: Phrygian dominant has a major 3rd instead of minor 3rd, creating an even more Spanish/Middle Eastern flavor
relatedScales.usage: More intensely exotic sound, common in flamenco and Middle Eastern music

relatedScales.differences: Dorian has a natural 2nd and natural 6th; Phrygian has flat 2nd and flat 6th for a much darker sound
relatedScales.usage: Sophisticated, jazzy minor sound compared to Phrygian's dark intensity
